correctness.rationale: The density definition requires uniform numerator p coprime to all sufficiently large q, a constant C and v∈T with 1<=v<q. For prime q, each fixed v<q covers O(q^(1-s)) reduced numerator classes; Bertrand extends T(q)≫_s q^s from primes to all Q, giving δ(T)<=liminf_Q log T(Q)/log Q. For 0<t<1, stages n_k=floor(2^(tk)),d_k=floor(2^k/n_k) produce S_t of O(Q^t) counting growth and Dirichlet guarantees a v=md_k<q at every q in (2^k,2^(k+1)] with fractional error <=1/(n_k+1), so δ(S_t)=t. Endpoint cores S0=∅ and S1=N are handled separately. Alternating b_{j+1}=2^(b_j) full blocks E and O=N\E cover N, each with upper ordinary density one and liminf logarithmic count exponent zero at alternate endpoints. Then Aα=E∪Sα and Bβ=O∪Sβ have lower δ from the core and upper δ from the sparse endpoint count, achieving exactly all (α,β). Independent exact-q tests for t=1/2 and q<121 support finite boundaries, not asymptotic conclusions.
residual_risks: This does not construct disjoint partitions with arbitrary strictly positive prescribed pairs; arbitrary real input may not be computationally effective.

value.rationale: Directly solves the open union question for the exact restricted Diophantine density proposed by Sanford 20 Oct 2026 and strengthens it to the entire [0,1]² pair spectrum under coverage with both upper ordinary densities 1. It identifies a maximal failure of subadditivity for a natural number-theoretic approximation invariant. Existing analytic ingredients do not make the resulting precise invariant worthless merely because the proof is short.
residual_risks: The result is a synthesis of known lemmas and an already-known block method; novelty at the joint consequence is bounded.

limitations: Not a disjoint partition theorem for arbitrary positive α,β; full prescribed pair spectrum only requires coverage.
